features.description: `apply` checks the cap per operation: the writes are ordered (delete, replace, anchored add, plain add), each tier-1 write is capChecked on its own and a breach drops that op alone with `over the cap: …`; `refused` retires from the result, the body and `memory_pr`; an anchored add on a file under both caps lands as a plain add, and a real eviction's body line and note name the evicted line.
steps: Written first and watched failing in tests/unit/curator.test.mjs: a 16th `## Gotchas` add without an anchor on a file at 15 is dropped with `over the cap: ## Gotchas: 16 entries, over 15` while a `replace` beside it lands (replacing `curator.mjs: a 16th Gotchas add without an anchor refuses the tier-1 commit, naming the breach`); the op that crosses 120 lines is dropped with `over the cap: CLAUDE.md: 121 lines, over 120` and the ops before and after it land (replacing `curator.mjs: a result over 120 lines refuses the tier-1 commit`); a `delete` and an anchorless `add` in one list on a file at 15 Gotchas both land, the delete first; a file over the cap takes its `replace` and `delete` and drops its anchorless `add` naming the cap (extending `curator.mjs: a file already over the cap takes a replace or a delete`); the result has no `refused` key; an anchored `add` on a file under both caps is appended with its anchor line kept (lib/memlint.mjs `gotchasDiff`: added 1, edited 0, deleted 0) and the same op on a file at 15 Gotchas evicts (edited 1); the replaced names leave tests/fixtures/check-names.txt and tests/fixtures/check-names-fast.txt in the same commit.

lib/curator.mjs: `apply` orders the writes (`delete`, `replace`, `add` with an anchor, `add` without, each group in file order: *default*) and runs `capCheck` on the one file's text before and after each tier-1 write, reverting a breaching op alone (`dropped` with `over the cap: …`) and trying the next op on the text before it; `write` appends an anchored `add` when the appended text passes `capCheck` and evicts the anchor's line only when it would not; an applied op that evicted carries `evicted` (the line it replaced, *default*); the result has no `refused` field; `body` has no `The tier-1 commit was refused` line and its *Applied (tier 1)* line reads `(in place of: <evicted line>)` for an eviction as for a `replace`, nothing of the kind for a plain add; `node --check lib/curator.mjs` passes.

lib/record.sh `memory_pr`: the refusal branch and the note `memory: tier-1 commit refused (…)` are gone; a cap drop is noted as every drop is (`memory: dropped add ## Gotchas (over the cap: ## Gotchas: 16 entries, over 15)`); an eviction is noted `memory: evicted "<line cut to 80>" for add ## Gotchas` (*default* wording); an `apply` that prints nothing is still `memory: apply failed (see run.log)`; `bash -n lib/record.sh` passes.

tests/fixtures/memory/stub-cap.json gains a second op, a `replace` of the seeded 2nd Gotchas line (`seeded gotcha 02`) with B's fact (`{{LINE:B}}`), and tests/fixtures/memory/README.md's line says so; tests/checks/memory-branch.sh's `mc` run gets `STUB_FACTS=A,B` and its check, written first: the run ends done with exactly one `memory: dropped add ## Gotchas (over the cap: ## Gotchas: 16 entries, over 15)` note, `harness-memory/mc` on origin one commit past main whose CLAUDE.md has 15 Gotchas lines with B's fact and without `seeded gotcha 02`, the `memory: mc` PR open with the dropped op under `## Dropped`, and no `tier-1 commit refused` note in its harness-log.md (replacing `memory PR: a 16th Gotchas add without an anchor refuses the tier-1 commit; no branch, no PR`); the `me` run's eviction check also reads `(in place of: - seeded gotcha 03` in the PR body's Applied section and the eviction note in harness-log.md.

`journal/decisions/2026-11-08-memory-rules-pr.md` is created (title, provenance: this run, the spec's N1 in docs/specs/2026-11-07-memory-followup.md, journal/learning/2026-11-07-memory-curator.md §12 answer 5) with N1-03's row: the per-op cap, the write order, the eviction only past the cap, `refused` retired, each *default* marked; `journal/decisions/2026-11-07-memory-tiers.md`'s cap answer gets one line saying N1-03 built it.

features.description: `.claude/CLAUDE.md` and `.claude/rules/` are project memory and guarded as such: `restrict … memory` reverts them, the curator's `FILES` and base take `.claude/CLAUDE.md`, and memlint lints the twin on its own cap and reports `twin` when both files exist.
steps: Written first and watched failing in tests/checks/memory-one-writer.sh (fast): the sourced `restrict … memory` case also adds `.claude/CLAUDE.md` and `.claude/rules/a/b.md` and edits `.claude/settings.json`, and the first two go back while the third stays (replacing `restrict memory: CLAUDE.md and .harness/project.md go back, added, edited or deleted; docs/CLAUDE.md, lib/ and .harness/config.sh stay` in tests/fixtures/check-names.txt and check-names-fast.txt); a stub run with `STUB_DOT_CLAUDE=A` (a new knob in tests/stub-claude.sh: that feature's first coding session writes `.claude/CLAUDE.md` and adds `.claude/rules/r.md`) ends done with neither file on the milestone branch `run/<run>/M1` nor on origin main and two revert notes, one naming `.claude/CLAUDE.md` and one `.claude/rules/r.md`.

Written first in tests/unit/curator.test.mjs: `validate` accepts `.claude/CLAUDE.md` as a `file` and refuses `.claude/rules/x.md` with a reason naming the three files; `capCheck` caps `.claude/CLAUDE.md` as it caps `CLAUDE.md`; `apply` writes a `## Gotchas` op into `.claude/CLAUDE.md`, and the CLI never writes through a symlinked `.claude/`. In tests/unit/memlint.test.mjs: `lint` finds `twin` (`.claude/CLAUDE.md:1 twin: CLAUDE.md exists too; Claude Code loads both as project memory`) when both exist and no `twin` with one, and lints `.claude/CLAUDE.md`'s size and Gotchas on their own cap.

tests/checks/memlint-run.sh (fast): a project with both files gets the `twin` note before the initializer's and `harness memlint <project>` prints it. tests/checks/memory-branch.sh: a run on a project whose memory is `.claude/CLAUDE.md` alone (no root CLAUDE.md) lands its facts in `.claude/CLAUDE.md` on `harness-memory/<run>`, folded into an existing seed when the file's time allows, else its own run.

lib/record.sh: `restrict`'s memory spec is `CLAUDE.md .harness/project.md .claude/CLAUDE.md .claude/rules` (the whole directory: *default*), `memory_base` copies `.claude/CLAUDE.md` into `$SCRATCH/memory-base/` when the base has it, `memory_foreign`'s path filter admits it; lib/curator.mjs `FILES` gains `.claude/CLAUDE.md` and `plain` reads it; lib/memlint.mjs runs `size`, `gotchas`, `derivable-count` and `run-scope` on `.claude/CLAUDE.md` on its own cap (*default*) and adds the `twin` finding; prompts/curator.md names `{{MEMORY_BASE}}/.claude/CLAUDE.md` when present; `.claude/rules/*.md` is guarded but no operation target (*default*); `bash -n lib/record.sh tests/stub-claude.sh` and `node --check lib/curator.mjs lib/memlint.mjs` pass.

`journal/decisions/2026-11-08-memory-rules-pr.md` gets N1-02's row with the documentation page cited (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory, read 2026-11-07), the four pathspecs, and what stays unguarded by choice (`CLAUDE.local.md`, the user's own rules directory), defaults marked; tests/stub-claude.sh's header gets the `STUB_DOT_CLAUDE` line; tests/fixtures/memory/README.md is updated where a fixture changed.
`bash tests/run.sh memory-one-writer memlint-run memory-branch` ends with every check passing (its `N/N checks passed` line).

features.description: Tier 2 lands on `harness-rules/<run>` with its own `memory rules: <run>` PR that the driver never merges: `apply` cuts `texts` and `ruleTexts` from one base under a union cap, `memory_pr` runs once per tier, `auto` merges the facts PR only, the bodies number every rule and proposal `<run>/<n>`, and `memory.json`, the report, `ledger/memory.jsonl` and `harness memory` count facts and rules apart.
steps: Written first and watched failing in tests/unit/curator.test.mjs: `apply` writes a tier-2 op into `ruleTexts` and not `texts`, a tier-1 op the reverse, `rules` holding the tier-2 ops in order and `proposed` tier 3 only (replacing `curator.mjs: only tier 1 is written; a tier-2 op leaves the texts as they were`); the union shadow drops a tier-2 `add` that would take the merged file past 120 lines while each tier alone fits, with `over the cap: CLAUDE.md: 121 lines, over 120`; a rules write that would change a protected section's raw lines is dropped; `body` renders the facts body, the rules body and the union, every tier-2 rule then tier-3 proposal numbered `<run>/<n>` in one sequence in the headings (`### 3 · add CLAUDE.md · ## Live system (entries.jsonl:7)`), the facts body ending `Rules of this run: <url>` (or `none`) and the rules body `Facts of this run: <url>` (replacing `curator.mjs: body lists the applied and tier-2 ops with their from, then the proposals, then the dropped with reasons`).

Written first in tests/unit/summary.test.mjs: `memoryState` reads `memory: <run>: 2 rules` commits as the driver's and `Merge branch 'main' into harness-rules/<run>` as neither; `memory-line` writes two rows for a summary with both PRs, each with `tier` (`facts` or `rules`) and `sections` (the `##` headings its ops touched), replacing by `url`; `memoryView` prints the tier in each line (`<run> · <project> · facts · 2/0/1 · <url> · open`, `<run> · <project> · rules · 1 · ## Code rules · <url> · open`) and one tally line per tier (`facts: merged unchanged a · edited b · closed c · open d`, then `rules: …`), a row without `tier` counted as facts.

Written first in tests/checks/memory-branch.sh: the `mp` run's `## Code rules` line is one commit `memory: mp: 1 rules` on `harness-rules/mp` and absent from `harness-memory/mp`, its PR is titled `memory rules: mp`, left for Michael, with `Facts of this run:` naming the facts PR in its body and `Rules of this run:` naming it in the facts PR's (replacing `memory PR: the workflow line is not committed and is in the PR body with its entries.jsonl line`); the record PR still opens; the notes read `memory: 3 ops · 2 facts · 1 rules · 0 dropped · 1 proposals`; `harness memory` lists two `mp` lines with `facts` and `rules` and two tally lines, and `ledger/memory.jsonl` has two `mp` rows with `tier` and `sections`; `mp`'s continue reuses the open rules PR (`gh pr edit` on its URL in its gh log); the `ma` run (auto) merges the facts PR and leaves the rules PR open with `memory rules PR opened; left for Michael · <url>` and no `gh pr merge` of its URL in its gh log; a `harness-rules/<run>` branch on origin with a commit the driver would not write stops the rules half with its note while the facts half lands; no run leaves a local `harness-rules/*` or `harness-memory/*` branch or a registered scratch worktree (replacing `memory PR: no run leaves its scratch worktree registered or a local harness-memory branch`); the report's `Memory` row reads `2 applied · 1 rules · 0 dropped · 1 proposals · PR <url> · rules PR <url>` and `memory-result.json` sits in the run record beside `memory-ops.json`.

lib/curator.mjs: `apply` returns `{texts, ruleTexts, rules, applied, proposed, dropped, rederived, run}`, both sets cut from the base, the write gate unchanged (a `proposed_changes` string never gates tier 1), the protected raw-line check on both, the per-op cap on tier 1 and then on the union shadow (tier 1's ops then tier 2's on one text); `memory-result.json` carries `ruleTexts` and the numbered items so `memory_pr`'s rules pass can write them into the recreated scratch worktree and N2-03 can name them (the CLI shape is the session's: *default*); `body` takes which body to render (facts, rules or the union for `memory.md`); `node --check lib/curator.mjs` passes.

lib/record.sh: `memory_pr` is one path run for `facts` (`harness-memory/<run>`, subject `memory: <run>: <n> facts`, title `memory: <run>`) and then `rules` (`harness-rules/<run>`, `memory: <run>: <n> rules`, `memory rules: <run>`), `memory_base` and `memory_foreign` taking the branch and the subject word, `memory_wt_gone` between the two passes (one worktree path reused: *default*), each push never forced, each PR opened or its body refreshed on a continue, a failure in one pass its own note that does not stop the other; `memory_merge` is called with the facts URL alone (`grep -n memory_merge lib/record.sh` shows no call on the rules path); a closed rules PR with its branch on origin stops the rules half with the delete-the-branch note; `memory_json` gains `rules` and `rules_pr`; the notes `memory rules PR opened; left for Michael · <url>`, `memory rules PR updated · <url>`, `memory rules PR: none (no tier-2 change)`; lib/driver.sh `curator()` copies `memory-result.json` into the run record; `bash -n lib/record.sh lib/driver.sh` passes.

lib/summary.mjs: `memoryOf` reads `rules` and `rules_pr`, `memoryLine` prints the report row, `memoryRow` gives one row per PR with `tier` and `sections`, `memoryState` reads the subject word, `memoryView` the tier and the two tallies; prompts/curator.md says tier 2 is a diff on `harness-rules/<run>` that Michael merges and the driver never does; templates/user/config.sh and templates/project/config.sh's `MEMORY_POLICY` comment says `auto` merges facts only; tests/fixtures/memory/README.md says stub-three-ops's `## Code rules` op lands on the rules branch; `journal/decisions/2026-11-08-memory-rules-pr.md` gets N1-01's rows (the sibling prefix `harness-rules/`, two text sets from one base, the union cap, facts first, the numbering, both bodies carrying tier 3 and the dropped ops, counted apart) and the three invariants each with the check that proves it, every *default* marked.

features.description: Review + simplify of N1 on Opus: a reviewer reads the milestone diff from a file and answers the five hard questions (the union cap, no merge of the rules PR under `auto`, the four pathspecs, every removed check name's successor, `harness memory` on a pre-N1 `memory.jsonl`); Critical/Important findings fixed RED→GREEN; simplifications applied; docs/architecture.md, README.md and the decision file describe N1 as built.
steps: The milestone diff is written to a file (`git diff $(git merge-base HEAD origin/main) -- lib prompts tests docs journal templates README.md > $HARNESS_SCRATCH/N1.diff`) and read by an Opus subagent, one round (a second only when the first finds something Critical), which answers with file and line: that the union shadow holds (two PRs each under the cap cannot merge into a file over 120 lines or 15 Gotchas); that no path lets the driver merge the rules PR under `MEMORY_POLICY=auto` (every `memory_merge` call in lib/record.sh named); that `restrict`'s four pathspecs revert nothing beside them (`.claude/settings.json` edited in a run survives); that every check name N1 removed has a successor named in `journal/decisions/2026-11-08-memory-rules-pr.md` (decisions/2026-11-03-trim's rule); that `harness memory` on a `memory.jsonl` written before N1 (rows without `tier`) still prints; its findings (Critical, Important, Minor, each with file, line and what was done) are in `docs/plans/2026-11-08-N1-review.md`.

Every Critical and Important finding is fixed with a failing test first (a unit test in tests/unit/ for a pure branch, a check in tests/checks/ for a driver behaviour) and then green; simplification passes are applied; `bash -n` passes on every shell file N1 touched and `node --check` on every `.mjs`.

docs/architecture.md: the component rows for lib/curator.mjs, lib/summary.mjs, lib/memory.sh and prompts/curator.md; the Memory curation state row (`memory-result.json` in the record, `memory.json`'s `rules` and `rules_pr`); the Memory PRs ledger row (`tier`, `sections`); the Project memory guard row names the four pathspecs; the Memory lint row the `twin` finding; the branches and PRs table gains `harness-rules/<run>` and PR `memory rules: <run>` (never merged by the driver); the CURATOR step (facts then rules, each op under the cap, a breaching one dropped); the `MEMORY_POLICY` row (`auto` merges facts only). README.md: *Memory curator*, *Memory lint*, the one-writer paragraph, `harness memory`'s tier lines.

`journal/decisions/2026-11-08-memory-rules-pr.md` is complete: title, provenance, finding, choice (N1-01, N1-02, N1-03 rows), rejected (`harness-memory/<run>/rules` as a ref, rules stacked on the facts commit, `.claude/rules/*.md` as an operation target, a cap budget shared across the twins, the whole-commit refusal); the N1 check names added, replaced and removed are counted against the budget of 50 (`git diff $(git merge-base HEAD origin/main) -- tests/fixtures/check-names.txt | grep -c '^+[^+]'` and `grep -c '^-[^-]'`) and the count, with any overrun's reason, is in the decision file and the entry's `checks` field.
`bash tests/run.sh` (in the background, a timeout of at least 1,500,000 ms) ends with every check passing (its `N/M checks passed` line with N = M); the suite is green.

features.description: The curator session runs under a deny list the driver passes: `session()` takes `S_DENY` and appends `--disallowedTools`, `curator()` fixes `CURATOR_DENY=("Bash(git push:*)" "Bash(gh:*)")`, the run.log line and one note say so, and the stub records every headless argv and skips its push when denied.
steps: Written first and watched failing in tests/checks/curator-run.sh: the `cu` run's curator argv (`$STUB_DIR/argv/<n>-curator.args`, the new record) has `--disallowedTools` followed by exactly `Bash(git push:*)` and `Bash(gh:*)`, and the same run's coding, verify and retro argv files have no `--disallowedTools` (*default*: the curator alone); its run.log line is `curator · <model> · deny Bash(git push:*) Bash(gh:*)` and harness-log.md has one `curator: session denied Bash(git push:*), Bash(gh:*)` note; a run with `STUB_CURATOR_PUSH=1` ends done with `harness-memory/<run>` holding the driver's one commit past main and no other, and its memory PR as tests/fixtures/memory/stub-three-ops.json predicts; tests/checks/queue-debrief.sh's `--disallowedTools` assertion is the model; the names go in tests/fixtures/check-names.txt.

tests/stub-claude.sh: every headless session records its argv in `$STUB_DIR/argv/<n>-<kind>.args` (the desk's `<n>-<name>.args` shape); `STUB_CURATOR_PUSH=1` has the stub curator commit a Gotchas line and push it to `harness-memory/<run>` unless its argv carries `--disallowedTools` with `Bash(git push:*)`, in which case it does not push; no denial event is printed (none captured from the real CLI: *default*); the header gets both lines; `bash -n tests/stub-claude.sh` passes.

lib/record.sh `session()`: `S_DENY` (an array, as `S_TURNS`, `S_BUDGET` and `S_TIMEOUT` are overrides) appended to the one `claude -p` line as `--disallowedTools "${S_DENY[@]}"` when set; lib/driver.sh `curator()`: `CURATOR_DENY=("Bash(git push:*)" "Bash(gh:*)")` beside `MAX_TURNS=40 SESSION_BUDGET_USD=3`, passed as `S_DENY`, the `log` line and the `note`; `grep -n S_DENY lib/*.sh` shows the curator as the only caller; prompts/curator.md keeps its no-push, no-`gh` sentence and adds that the driver denies them; `bash -n lib/record.sh lib/driver.sh` passes.

features.description: Review + simplify of N2 on Opus: a reviewer reads the milestone diff from a file and answers the five hard questions (no merge without the refreshed body, the deny list on the curator's `claude` line alone, the answers match by key, a replaced verdict counted once, `harness memory` without an answers file); Critical/Important findings fixed RED→GREEN; simplifications applied; docs/architecture.md, README.md and the decision file describe N2 as built.
steps: The milestone diff is written to a file (`git diff $(git merge-base HEAD origin/main) -- lib bin prompts tests docs journal templates README.md > $HARNESS_SCRATCH/N2.diff`) and read by an Opus subagent, one round (a second only when the first finds something Critical), which answers with file and line: that no path merges a PR whose body refresh failed (the edit's status is read where the merge decides); that the deny list reaches the real `claude` line in `session()` for the curator and no other role (the stub's argv for the curator, `grep -n S_DENY lib/*.sh` for the rest); that the accept/decline match is by `key` and cannot drop a tier-1 op or a different sentence; that a replaced verdict is counted once; that `harness memory`'s listing runs with an empty or missing `memory-answers.jsonl`; its findings (Critical, Important, Minor, each with file, line and what was done) are in `docs/plans/2026-11-08-N2-review.md`.

Every Critical and Important finding is fixed with a failing test first (a unit test in tests/unit/ for a pure branch, a check in tests/checks/ for a driver behaviour) and then green; simplification passes are applied; `bash -n` passes on every shell file N2 touched and `node --check` on every `.mjs`.

docs/architecture.md: the Read-only sessions guard row says the curator also runs under `--disallowedTools`; the CURATOR step carries the deny list, the answers file and the merge only with the body; the `MEMORY_POLICY` row and the PR table say the facts PR is merged only with its body on it; the ledger files table gains `memory-answers.jsonl`; lib/memory.sh's and lib/curator.mjs's rows name the verbs, `answers` and the two drop reasons. README.md: *Memory curator*'s `auto` sentence, `harness memory`'s row with `proposals`, `accept` and `decline`.

`journal/decisions/2026-11-08-memory-session-and-answers.md` is complete: title, provenance, finding, choice (N2-01, N2-02, N2-03 rows), rejected (a `--settings` JSON deny list, a retry of the edit inside the segment, a verdict matched by section, a copy of the answers in the run record); the N2 check names added, replaced and removed are counted against the budget of 30 (`git diff $(git merge-base HEAD origin/main) -- tests/fixtures/check-names.txt | grep -c '^+[^+]'` and `grep -c '^-[^-]'`) and the count, with any overrun's reason, is in the decision file and the entry's `checks` field.
`bash tests/run.sh` (in the background, a timeout of at least 1,500,000 ms) ends with every check passing (its `N/M checks passed` line with N = M); the suite is green.
